claim_set.claim_text: Every AI-assisted privilege determination, production / withholding decision, or research assertion that moves toward a consequential litigation action (entering a privilege log, releasing a production set, withholding a document, certifying a discovery response) MUST map to a recorded named-authority decision — the agent, the determination artefact, the intended consequential action, and the named supervising attorney / privilege-review lead under whose authority it proceeds. Determinations lacking a recorded authority decision are refused at the action-admissibility gate.

Before an AI-reviewed document proceeds to a consequential litigation action it MUST carry a recorded discovery chain-of-custody — the source custodian and collection point, every transformation (de-duplication, redaction, format conversion, AI classification) with actor and timestamp, and the integrity hash as collected and as produced — so the document can be authenticated under FRE 901/902 and the disclosure certified as complete and reasonable under FRCP 26(g) / CPR PD 57AD.

Every AI-asserted fact, case citation, document characterisation, or privilege rationale that proceeds toward a consequential litigation action MUST emit a signed, replay-derivable provenance pin binding the generating model and version, the inputs, the pinned source for each asserted fact or citation, the review basis applied, and the named-authority outcome — so no AI-asserted fact or citation is relied on without a pinned, verifiable source (the no-hallucinated-citation rule the Mata v. Avianca fake-citation sanctions made non-negotiable). An assertion without a resolvable pinned source is refused and never proceeds.

Every AI-reviewed item that proceeds to a consequential litigation action MUST emit a signed, replay-provable litigation Evidence Pack binding the named-authority decision, the recorded chain-of-custody, the pinned-source provenance, and the review basis under a context seal — reconstructable and valid at T=0, derivable from published keys alone, retained under WORM — the defensibility artefact a court, opposing counsel, or a regulator can verify offline when the AI-assisted work is challenged.

Every AI-assisted litigation determination that proceeds to a consequential action MUST carry a contestability record — a stable determination identifier, the inputs and authority and evidence it rested on, and a reconstruction / challenge route — so that when the determination is challenged in court (a privilege clawback under FRE 502, a motion to compel, a spoliation / sanctions inquiry under FRCP 37, a disclosure challenge under CPR PD 57AD) it can be reconstructed exactly as made and contested through a recorded route.

KYE governs the AUTHORITY + EVIDENCE + DEFENSIBILITY of AI-assisted litigation work and PROVES it for litigation — who authorised the privilege call, the provenance of the AI review, the chain-of-custody, whether it can be reconstructed and contested. KYE does NOT do legal research, judge the legal merits, write the brief, render the privilege opinion, or replace counsel.
